transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been doing some things that don’t feel like me. Walking out in the middle of deployments at work, driving around late at night with no real plan. It scares me a bit, honestly. I’ve never handled stress like this before.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself do these things?
I… don’t think so. Not exactly. It’s more like I realize afterward what I did, but I don’t feel like I’m watching myself from the outside.
Do you feel like you're in control of your actions when you're doing these things that don't feel like you?

Not really. I mean… I’m physically doing it, so I guess I’m choosing it in the moment, but it doesn’t feel like me. Walking out during deployments, or driving around late with nowhere to go… afterward I think, why did I do that? It scares me.
Do you have any memories that you can't explain or gaps in your memory from the times when you were doing these things that didn't feel like you?

Yeah… there are parts I can’t really account for. I remember some things almost too clearly, like the contractor’s face and the noise, but then there’s this chunk in the middle where I know I was there… I just can’t pull it back.
Do you often find yourself unable to recall things that happened during these episodes?

Often enough that it bothers me. I’ll remember certain parts really sharply… like his face, the noise. But then there’s this middle part that’s just missing. I know I was there, I just… can’t get it back.
Are these episodes of doing things that don't feel like you often triggered by something emotionally upsetting or stressful?

Yeah… usually when I’m stressed. It’s like something builds up and then I just do something stupid, like leave during a deployment or drive around at night with no plan. That’s not how I used to handle things.
Do you ever feel confused about who you are or what's happening to you during these episodes?
I don’t know… not exactly confused about who I am. More like I feel off, like I’m not fully tracking what’s happening. It’s hard to explain.
Do you ever feel like you have different parts of yourself that are in conflict with each other?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean… I argue with myself sometimes, but I don’t know about “different parts.” It’s more just feeling pulled in different directions, I guess.
Do you ever feel like there's more than one version of you, or that you're not always the same person?
I don’t really think of it that way. I mean, I can feel different depending on what’s going on, but not like… more than one me. Not that I’ve noticed.
Do you find that you forget things you did or learned before these episodes happened?
Some of it, yeah. I remember certain parts really clearly… like the contractor’s face, and the noise. But there’s this part in the middle where I know I was there, and I just… can’t get it back.
Do you ever feel uncertain about your own identity or question who you really are?
Not really. I mean… I don’t sit around wondering who I am. I get confused about things sometimes, but not my identity, I don’t think.
Do you feel a sense of detachment from yourself or your surroundings when you're doing these things that don't feel like you?
I’m not sure. Maybe a little… like things feel sort of distant sometimes. But I wouldn’t say I’m outside myself or anything. It’s hard to explain.
Do you experience intense fear or anxiety when you realize what you've done during these episodes?
Yes. When I realize I’ve done something like… leaving in the middle of a deployment, or driving around late at night with nowhere to go, it scares me. That’s not how I usually handle things.
Do you feel like you're spaced out or disconnected from the world around you when these things are happening?
I don’t know. Maybe a little, but I’m not really aware of it while it’s happening. It’s more like afterward I realize something was off.
Do you find that there are periods of time in your life that you cannot remember, even when things were not particularly stressful?
Not that I can think of. I mean, I forget normal things sometimes, but I don’t think I have whole periods missing when nothing stressful was going on.
Do you often find yourself discovering things you've done or said that you don't remember?
Not really. I mean… I haven’t noticed people telling me I said things I don’t remember. Maybe little things, but nothing that stands out.
Do you feel like you're disconnected from your thoughts or feelings when you're doing these things that don't feel like you?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it that way in the moment. It’s more like… I just don’t feel quite myself, but I can’t say I’m disconnected from my thoughts or feelings exactly.
Do you feel like you're in a dream-like state when you're doing these things that don't feel like you?
I don’t think so. Not like a dream, exactly. Sometimes things feel… off, but I wouldn’t say dream-like.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your actions during these episodes?

I wouldn’t say I’m totally unable to control myself. It’s more… I’ve been doing things that scare me after, like leaving in the middle of a deployment or driving around late at night with nowhere to go. It doesn’t feel like how I usually handle things.
Do you experience memory gaps for everyday events, not just the episodes where you did things that didn't feel like you?
I don’t think so. I mean, I forget normal things sometimes, but not… gaps, like losing chunks of the day. At least not that I’ve noticed.
